title: Occupancy-smoothing prefetch throttles and canary fallbacks for OOM resilience
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Production clusters are experiencing intermittent OOMs under mixed workloads with long-chat and short-chat traffic cohabiting the same GPU pools. Root causes include bursty prefix-heavy requests that prefetch large KV blobs, uneven continuous-batching admission that oversubscribes memory, and slow kernel swaps (quantized vs FP16) that transiently inflate working set.

Goal: Add a multilayered runtime protocol — occupancy-smoothing admission, prefetch throttles with per-session budgets, kernel-aware admission heuristics, and a controlled canary fallback path to compact model variants — to prevent OOMs and recover gracefully when memory pressure spikes. The solution should preserve quality for high-SLA customers while keeping token costs predictable.

Scope: Engineering runtime + scheduler + KV manager. Deliverables include an admission policy implementation, prefetch budget accounting, a staged KV demotion and snapshot plan (GPU->CPU->disk), a canary fallback flow to tiny/quantized model variants, observability (traces/metrics/dashboards), and an ops runbook for incidents and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: New occupancy-smoothing admission reduces concurrent GPU working-set variance by >= 45% in synthetic mixed workload tests
End-to-end system OOM rate on canary clusters decreases by >= 90% compared to baseline for 72h soak
P95 generation latency regression <= 10% for P95-sensitive routes (high-tier customers) under median load
Prefetch budget prevents any single session from allocating > 30% of a slot's prefetchable KV without explicit override
Fallback flow succeeds in under 250ms for admission-triggered model swap and continues streaming partial response where possible
Dashboard with new heatmap and sentinel metrics (occupancy_variance, prefetched_bytes_per_session, fallback_invocations) published and linked in the ticket
Automated e2e test that injects KV-snapshot failure and verifies graceful degrade path is present in CI

notes: Key engineering trade-offs discussed: aggressive prefetch truncation reduces quality for long conversational sessions; to mitigate we expose per-customer prefetch overrides gated by quota and require ops approval. Kernel-aware checks rely on a maintained kernel profile registry that must be kept in sync with model onboarding flow.
runbook: Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Occupancy+Smoothing+Runbook. Key steps: 1) detect rising occupancy_variance > threshold, 2) enable emergency prefetch throttle for offending sessions, 3) trigger staged KV demotion, 4) if demotion fails, route new requests for affected slot to fallback tiny-quant model and mark timeframe for replay, 5) alert on fallback_invocations > 5% for > 15m
customer_notes: Customer-facing summary (for on-call): We will deploy an admission controller and per-session prefetch budgets. In rare cases we may swap to a compact variant with slightly lower output fidelity to avoid timeouts. Enterprise customers can opt into larger reserved slots to reduce swap frequency.
